transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my sleep has gotten really messed up. I work overnight shifts, and even after I get off I’ll just lie there wide awake. Then if I do finally fall asleep, I wake up scared, and it feels like I didn’t rest at all.
Do you have these scary waking experiences frequently?
Yeah, it happens a lot. After my overnight shifts I’ll be exhausted, but I still just lie there awake. And if I do fall asleep, I wake up scared, like I didn’t really sleep at all.
Do you have bad dreams when you wake up scared?

I don’t know if they’re exactly bad dreams. I just know when I finally drift off, I wake up scared, like I didn’t get any real rest. My sleep feels all broken up, especially after my overnight shifts.
Do you remember what happens in the moments right before you wake up scared?

I don’t really remember anything clear right before. It’s more like I finally doze off after lying there awake from work, and then I just wake up scared. I can’t say what happens before it—I just know I don’t feel rested at all.
Do you experience these sleep disturbances and scary waking experiences on your days off from work as well?

Yeah, even on my days off it can happen. It’s worse after the overnight shifts, but my sleep is just broken up now. I’ll lie there wide awake, and then if I do drift off, I wake up scared and feel like I didn’t really rest.
Do you think your overnight shifts or the stress from work is contributing to your sleep problems?

Yeah, I think the overnight shifts are part of it. I’ll get off work and I’m exhausted, but then I’m still just lying there wide awake. And when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up scared, like I didn’t rest at all. It feels like my sleep is just all broken up now.
Do you feel stressed or anxious about work when you lie awake at night?

Yeah… I think so. When I get off an overnight shift I’m exhausted, but I still just lie there wide awake. My sleep’s all broken up, and if I do drift off, I wake up scared and it feels like I never really rested.
Do you often feel extremely tired or sleepy during the day?

Yeah, I do. I feel really worn out during the day, like I never actually slept. Even when I’m exhausted after work, I’ll be wide awake, and then if I do fall asleep I wake up scared, so it doesn’t feel restful at all.
Have you experienced any traumatic events recently or in the past that might be connected to your sleep problems?
I don’t think so. I mean, nothing really comes to mind that I’d call traumatic. I’m not sure what it would be connected to, honestly.
Do you have trouble concentrating or performing daily tasks because of how you're sleeping?

Yes. I’m having a hard time keeping up with my care visits safely now. There was a care-plan visit where I got so overwhelmed and stuck that my supervisor had to stop me because I couldn’t finish it.

And outside of work, I’ve pulled away from church, Zumba, and mentoring. I can barely manage getting through work and getting home.
Are you avoiding certain activities or places because of the scary waking experiences or your overall sleep situation?

Yeah… I guess I am. I’ve stopped going to church, and I’m not doing Zumba or mentoring anymore. I just don’t feel like I can handle much outside of work.

Even work has been hard. I can’t really keep up with my care visits safely like before, and during one care-plan visit I got so overwhelmed and stuck that my supervisor had to stop me because I couldn’t finish it. Most days I’m just trying to get through work and get back home.
Do you have nightmares?

Not really nightmares like a story I remember. It’s more that when I finally do fall asleep, I wake up scared, like something’s wrong. My sleep is all broken up, and even after an overnight shift I’ll lie there wide awake. Then if I drift off, I wake up feeling like I didn’t rest at all.
Is there something specific that's stressing you out or worrying you when you're lying awake at night?

Yeah… it’s mostly work. I keep thinking I missed something in the care notes or did something wrong with a client.

Even when my supervisor tells me the notes are fine, I still feel like… no, I know I missed something, and that somebody got hurt because of me. Like they just haven’t told me yet. That’s what keeps going through my head when I’m lying there.
Do you feel like you're constantly thinking about work or replaying interactions with clients over and over in your head?

Yes. I replay everything, over and over. Every little thing I think I did wrong with patients… and even with my family.

It’s like I can’t let it go. I keep thinking I’m a worthless aide, like I should’ve protected people better. And I feel like God is mad at me for failing them.
Do you wake up scared with any specific thought or image in your mind?

Not really a clear picture or anything. I just wake up scared, like something is wrong. My sleep’s been all broken up… even after I get off an overnight shift, I’ll be lying there wide awake. And if I do drift off, I wake up feeling like I didn’t rest at all.
Do you wake up scared feeling guilty about something?

Yes… a lot of the time. I wake up feeling guilty, like I did something wrong or failed somebody. I start going over things I did with patients, or with my family, and it feels like I’m just a worthless aide. Like I should’ve protected people better… and like God is mad at me for that.
Is there something specific that you feel guilty about when you wake up scared?

It’s not usually one single thing. It’s more like… I wake up and start thinking about every little mistake I might’ve made with patients, or with my family. I feel like I failed them somehow, like I should’ve protected people better. And then it turns into feeling like I’m just a worthless aide… and like God is mad at me for it.
Is the feeling of guilt you experience when you wake up scared related to something specific that happened or is it a more general feeling?

It’s more general, I think. It’s not one specific thing that happened. I just start going over every little thing I might’ve done wrong, with patients or with my family, and it feels like I failed them. Like I’m a worthless aide… and like God is mad at me for not protecting people better.
Do you feel guilty about failing in your role as a care aide when you wake up scared?

Yes. I do. When I wake up like that, I start thinking about every little thing I might’ve done wrong with patients or with my family. It feels like I failed them, like I’m a worthless aide… and like God is mad at me for not protecting people better.
Do you feel like you have to repeat certain actions or thoughts to try and relieve the guilty feelings you have?
I don’t think so… not like a certain thing I have to repeat. I mostly just lie there thinking about it, feeling bad. I haven’t noticed myself doing any special action to make it go away.
